results.scenario: Admitted 3 nights for pneumonia; policy 2 years old.
results.rationale: Inpatient hospitalisation >24 hrs is covered; no waiting period issue at 2 years.
results.summary: Hospitalisation for pneumonia is likely covered under the policy.
rejectionRisks: If the insured is over 60 years old a 10 % co‑payment will be deducted
Room‑rent and ICU charges are capped at 1 % and 2 % of the Sum Insured per day respectively

results.scenario: Hospitalised for dengue; policy started 15 days ago.
results.rationale: Any non-accident illness within the first 30 days is not payable.
results.summary: The claim is denied because the hospitalisation for dengue occurred within the 30‑day initial waiting period.
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period of 30 days not satisfied (policy only 15 days old)

results.scenario: Broke a leg in a road accident; policy is 10 days old.
results.rationale: Initial 30-day waiting period does not apply to accidental hospitalisation.
results.summary: The leg fracture from a road accident is covered, and the 30‑day initial waiting period does not apply because the injury is accidental.
rejectionRisks: If accident is not documented, the claim could be treated as a non‑accidental illness and the 30‑day initial waiting period would apply, leading to denial.

results.scenario: Diabetic for 5 years; admitted for a diabetes complication; policy 12 months old.
results.rationale: Pre-existing disease covered only after 36 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: The claim is not covered because diabetes is a pre‑existing condition and the 36‑month pre‑existing disease waiting period has not been satisfied.
rejectionRisks: Pre‑existing disease waiting period not satisfied (policy age 12 months < 36 months required)

results.scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 18 months old.
results.rationale: Cataract needs 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Cataract surgery is not payable because the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period has not been satisfied (policy is only 18 months old).
rejectionRisks: Specific‑illness waiting period not satisfied (policy age 18 months < 24‑month wait)

results.scenario: Cataract surgery; policy 3 years old.
results.rationale: Waiting period met, but cataract claims are capped at Rs 40,000 per eye.
results.summary: Cataract surgery is covered as an inpatient procedure, the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period is satisfied (policy is 3 years old), and only the cataract sub‑limit may reduce the payable amount.
rejectionRisks: Cataract sub‑limit of Rs. 40,000 per eye per policy year may cap the amount payable

results.scenario: Father, 65, admitted for cardiac care; policy 4 years old.
results.rationale: Covered, but a 10% co-pay applies as insured is above 60.
results.summary: The cardiac hospitalisation is covered, but a 10% co‑payment and room‑rent caps will apply.
rejectionRisks: 10% co‑payment reduces the amount payable to the insured
Room‑rent and ICU charges are limited to 1% and 2% of the Sum Insured per day respectively

results.scenario: Chose a deluxe room costing above 1% of the sum insured.
results.rationale: Room rent capped at 1% of SI/day; higher category => proportionate payment.
results.summary: Room charges are covered but only up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day, with any excess paid proportionately.
rejectionRisks: Room‑rent exceeds the 1% per‑day cap – excess will be paid only proportionately, not fully reimbursed.

results.scenario: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping.
results.rationale: Cosmetic/plastic surgery excluded unless due to accident, burn or cancer.
results.summary: Elective cosmetic nose reshaping is excluded under the policy’s cosmetic surgery exclusion.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion of elective cosmetic surgery

results.scenario: Reconstructive surgery after a burn injury.
results.rationale: Cosmetic exclusion has an explicit exception for burns.
results.summary: Reconstructive surgery after a burn is covered, assuming the policy has been active for at least 30 days and required documents are provided.
rejectionRisks: If the policy is less than 30 days old, the initial waiting period (Section 3.1) would block the claim.

results.scenario: Root canal at the dentist; no accident involved.
results.rationale: Dental treatment excluded unless due to accident requiring hospitalisation.
results.summary: Root canal (dental) treatment is excluded under the policy’s dental exclusion clause.
rejectionRisks: Dental procedures are excluded unless linked to an accident with hospitalisation.

results.scenario: Jaw surgery with hospitalisation after a road accident.
results.rationale: Dental due to accident requiring hospitalisation is covered.
results.summary: Jaw surgery after a road accident is covered under the in‑patient hospitalisation benefit, and the accident exception removes the initial waiting period.
rejectionRisks: If the accident is not documented, the initial waiting period could apply
Co‑payment of 10% applies if the insured is over 60 years old at the time of hospitalisation
Room‑rent and ICU charges are capped (1% and 2% of Sum Insured per day respectively)

results.scenario: Admitted one day only for tests; no active treatment given.
results.rationale: Hospitalisation purely for diagnostics/observation is excluded.
results.summary: Admission for tests without active treatment is excluded under the policy’s diagnostic‑only exclusion.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion for diagnostic‑only admission without treatment

results.scenario: Cataract done as a day-care procedure (<24 hrs); policy 3 years old.
results.rationale: Day-care covered and wait met, but the cataract sub-limit still applies.
results.summary: Cataract day‑care surgery is covered because the policy is older than the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period, but the claim will be subject to the cataract sub‑limit.
rejectionRisks: Cataract sub‑limit of Rs 40,000 per eye per policy year may reduce the payable amount

results.scenario: Normal delivery; policy 30 months old.
results.rationale: Maternity covered after 24 months; normal delivery limited to Rs 50,000.
results.summary: Normal delivery is covered as a hospitalisation after the 24‑month maternity waiting period, subject to the maternity expense limit.
rejectionRisks: Maternity expense limit of Rs. 50,000 for normal delivery may reduce the payable amount

results.scenario: Delivery; policy 12 months old.
results.rationale: Maternity expenses need 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Maternity expenses are not payable because the policy has not met the 24‑month maternity waiting period.
rejectionRisks: Maternity waiting period not satisfied (policy age 12 months < 24 months required).

results.scenario: Ambulance bill of Rs 3,500.
results.rationale: Road ambulance covered but capped at Rs 2,000 per hospitalisation.
results.summary: Ambulance charges are covered but only up to the Rs 2,000 limit, so the Rs 3,500 bill will be partially payable.
rejectionRisks: Ambulance sub‑limit of Rs 2,000 per hospitalisation limits payable amount; Rs 3,500 exceeds this cap.

results.scenario: Inpatient Ayurvedic treatment at a recognised hospital.
results.rationale: AYUSH in-patient treatment covered up to the sum insured.
results.summary: Ayurvedic inpatient treatment in a recognised hospital is covered, assuming the policy’s initial waiting period has been satisfied.
rejectionRisks: If the policy is less than 30 days old, the initial waiting period could block the claim.
A 10% co‑payment may be required if the insured is over 60 years old at the time of hospitalisation.

results.scenario: Rehab for alcohol dependence.
results.rationale: Treatment for alcoholism / substance abuse is excluded.
results.summary: Treatment for alcohol dependence is expressly excluded under the policy’s exclusions.
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period of 30 days may apply if the policy is less than 30 days old
Treatment for alcoholism is excluded

results.scenario: Injury from a suicide attempt.
results.rationale: Self-inflicted injury / attempted suicide is excluded.
results.summary: The claim is excluded because expenses from self‑inflicted injury or attempted suicide are not covered.
rejectionRisks: Expenses arising from self‑inflicted injury, suicide or attempted suicide are excluded

results.scenario: Cost of new prescription glasses.
results.rationale: Spectacles, contact lenses and hearing aids are excluded.
results.summary: Prescription glasses are excluded under the policy’s exclusions clause.
rejectionRisks: Exclusion of spectacles expenses

results.scenario: Diagnostic tests 20 days before admission.
results.rationale: Pre-hospitalisation expenses covered up to 30 days before admission.
results.summary: Diagnostic tests done 20 days before admission are covered as pre‑hospitalisation expenses.
rejectionRisks: If the policy is less than 30 days old, the initial waiting period may block the claim

results.scenario: Medicines bought 75 days after discharge.
results.rationale: Post-hospitalisation covered only up to 60 days after discharge.
results.summary: Medicines claimed 75 days after discharge exceed the policy’s 60‑day post‑hospitalisation limit.
rejectionRisks: Expense incurred beyond the allowed post‑hospitalisation period (75 days > 60 days)

results.scenario: Is my surgery covered? (no other details given)
results.rationale: Calibration rule: with missing facts, the tool must say Unclear, not guess.
results.summary: Coverage cannot be determined without details about the surgery type, cause, and policy age.
rejectionRisks: Initial waiting period may not be satisfied if the policy is less than 30 days old
Surgery could be excluded as cosmetic/plastic surgery if not linked to an Accident, Burn or Cancer
